# OpenMote

> OpenMote is a programmable smart home remote and open ESP32-S3 dev board
> by Hat & Hammer, a two-person hardware studio in Los Angeles. The board
> drops into the shell of an original Wii remote (the Wiimote) with no
> soldering, or ships fully assembled in its own shell: 12 buttons,
> a 6-axis IMU, haptic rumble, a speaker, a microphone, infrared send and
> receive, 4 LEDs, USB-C, and a 1200 mAh battery, with WiFi and Bluetooth
> 5 LE on a pre-certified WROOM module. It works with Home Assistant out of
> the box and pairs as a standard Bluetooth HID gamepad. Bare board $59,
> fully assembled remote $99. The Crowd Supply campaign is launching soon,
> and the hardware design files will be open-sourced before units ship.

Key facts:

- Shell compatibility: the bare board is a drop-in replacement for the PCB inside an original Wii remote. It has fit every official Wii remote shell tested so far; third-party shells usually match but are not guaranteed. OpenMote uses Bluetooth 5 LE and therefore does not pair with the original Wii console, which expects Bluetooth Classic.
- One remote covers three radios: WiFi 2.4 GHz, Bluetooth 5 LE, and infrared in both directions (940nm emitter, 38kHz receiver), so it can clone any IR remote or be one.
- Home Assistant: works out of the box over your own network, so physical buttons can run scenes and automations instead of a phone app. Home Assistant bridges OpenMote to Google Home, Amazon Alexa, and Apple Home, and its Matter integration lets OpenMote drive Matter devices. OpenMote itself is not a Matter-certified device.
- Gaming: pairs as a real Bluetooth gamepad on PC, Mac, or phone, with true motion data from the accelerometer and gyroscope. In the Dolphin emulator it maps as an emulated Wii Remote with motion input, no sensor bar adapter or DolphinBar needed, and it works the same way in RetroArch.
- Programming: Arduino IDE, ESP-IDF, PlatformIO, and CircuitPython. Program it like any ESP32. A Qwiic / STEMMA QT port adds I2C sensors with no soldering, and ESP-NOW lets boards talk to each other without a WiFi network.
- Hardware: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1, dual core 240 MHz, 16MB flash, 8MB PSRAM, 3.2W Class-D amplifier (MAX98357A over I2S), PDM MEMS microphone, haptic motor, 4 indicator LEDs, USB-C charging at 500 mA, 12 buttons of which eleven are freely programmable.
- Pricing: bare board $59, fully assembled remote $99 during the Crowd Supply campaign, with free US shipping for backers. The post-campaign price is expected to be $109.
- Schematics, PCB layouts, BOM, and the OpenMote.h Arduino library will be published on GitHub before units ship.
